summary: Dedicated capacity: sustained throughput drag after burst due to uneven GPU credit drain and sidecar IO pressure
description:
Issue summary: Customer AcmeRetail reports a prolonged throughput and p99 latency degradation on their dedicated pool following a high-concurrency burst window on 2026-03-12 morning. Impact: sustained token/sec drop (~35% p50 throughput reduction) and p99 latency increase from ~200ms to ~1.1s for batched routes. Behavior persisted despite apparent GPU allocation availability (slots shown as free).

Observed: - Autoscaler did not immediately provision additional GPUs after the burst recovery window; many requests queued and experienced attach timeouts or long attach latencies. - GPU util% on affected nodes low-to-moderate (30–60%), but kernel stalls and PCIe/host IO wait spiked. - One tenant's sidecar was producing heavy checkpointing/diagnostic uploads during the recovery window, and node-local nvme and PCIe stalls correlate with throughput drag.

Why unique: Unlike classic slot exhaustion, this case shows apparent slot availability with poor effective throughput due to IO pressure and asymmetric GPU 'credit' depletion on a subset of nodes, causing allocator to overestimate usable capacity and autoscaler to delay scale-up.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route a phased burst (many short streams + some long streams) to a small dedicated pool (3 GPUs) pinned to tenant AcmeRetail.
2) Trigger a sidecar-heavy operation on one tenant instance that performs frequent state uploads (simulated diagnostic snapshot every 10s) while the burst is ongoing.
3) Observe allocator slot counts, attach latencies, and autoscaler decisions during burst and 30 minutes after burst.
4) Compare p99 latencies, GPU util, and host IO wait across nodes (node with noisy sidecar vs clean nodes).
observed_behavior: After burst, the allocator reports available slots and autoscaler remains in cooldown. However attach latencies remain high (1-2s) and many short streams queue. GPU utilization is inconsistent; the noisy node exhibits low kernel utilization but high host IO wait and NVME write latency. Customers see persistent p99 latency regression and throughput loss despite no formal 'slot exhaustion' alert.
expected_behavior: Autoscaler should either provision capacity when effective attach latency exceeds threshold despite free slots, or allocator should mark affected nodes as degraded so traffic can be routed off until IO pressure clears. Throughput should return to pre-burst baselines within autoscale recovery window (~5–10 minutes) unless constrained by real GPU shortages.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:18: Support alerted after customer reported p99 > 1s across multiple routes.
Checked autoscaler logs: autoscaler remained in cooldown and saw slot counts > 0; decision rule was "scale if free_slots < threshold" (threshold not breached).
Telemetry: attach_latency metric spiked on node-3 to median 1.2s; other nodes stayed ~120ms.
Node diagnostics: node-3 nvme write latency 40ms (baseline 2–5ms), host iowait elevated, PCIe write stalls observed in kernel logs (dmesg shows repeated PCIe DPC warnings).
Sidecar logs: a background snapshot service (customer sidecar v2.3.1) performed batched uploads every 10s during the window; throughput to local disk peaked and upload threads saturated NVME queue.

Hypothesis A: IO-heavy sidecar activity caused host-level stalls preventing normal kernel dispatch, reducing effective GPU throughput (low util but high stalls), causing perceived free slots that are not actually usable.

Hypothesis B: GPU credit accounting on allocator counts slots by allocation metadata without verifying attach latencies/health; allocator returned slots while node could not honor new attach requests quickly.
Quick test: cordon node-3 from serving and reroute traffic -> observed immediate drop in attach latency and throughput recovered to baseline within 3 minutes.
customer_communications: 2026-03-12 09:25 — Support (Aisha): 'Thanks for the report — we're investigating. Can you confirm whether you recently enabled snapshotting or added diagnostic uploads on your sidecar? Any recent deploys?'

2026-03-12 09:47 — AcmeRetail (Elena M.): 'We deployed sidecar v2.3.1 yesterday which includes periodic state snapshots for resilience. We haven't seen this behavior before. We're happy to pause snapshots if needed.'

2026-03-12 10:05 — Support (Liam): 'We're seeing host IO pressure on one of the pool nodes correlated with your snapshot schedule. We're going to drain that node and monitor. We'll coordinate a safe pause window for your snapshots.'
2026-03-12 10:12 — AcmeRetail: 'Pausing snapshots now; let us know when you reroute.'
2026-03-12 10:18 — Support: 'We drained node-3 and observed p99 drop back toward normal. Continuing to monitor and will keep this ticket open for postmortem and permanent mitigation.'
actions_taken: 2026-03-12 10:15 — Cordoned and drained node-3 from serving pool (allocator aware); re-routed traffic to remaining nodes.
2026-03-12 10:20 — Coordinated with customer to pause sidecar snapshot uploads; NVME latency returned toward baseline within ~4 minutes.

2026-03-12 11:00 — Temporarily increased autoscaler sensitivity to attach_latency metric via a control-plane patch (emergency config) so autoscaler will trigger scale-up when attach_latency > 500ms for >2min.
2026-03-12 13:30 — Rolled a fix to allocator health checks to include attach_latency/host_io_wait as criteria before advertising free_slots (canary to 5% of dedicated pools).
resolution_notes: Mitigation: Drained the affected node and paused customer snapshot uploads; throughput recovered. Short-term fix: autoscaler config adjusted to consider attach latency. Long-term fix: allocator change merged to include attach latency and host_io_wait in health scoring; will roll to production next week. Customer follow-up: AcmeRetail will update sidecar to rate-limit uploads and add jitter to snapshot schedule. Ticket remains In Progress until allocator change is fully rolled out and customer confirms no recurrence.
postmortem_followups: 1) Add attach_latency and host_io_wait health signals to allocator slot advertisement (PR merged, rollout scheduled).
2) Add a dedicated monitor and alert for mismatches between free_slot_count and attach_latency across a pool.
3) Docs: update Runbook 'Dedicated pool: IO-heavy sidecar detection' and provide sample sidecar rate-limiting config to customers.
4) Product: consider autoscaler policy to temporarily mark nodes 'degraded' and force immediate surge capacity when attach_latency persists.
5) Customer action: AcmeRetail will ship sidecar v2.3.2 with upload backoff; Support to validate next burst window.
6) QA: schedule synthetic burst test against canary allocator that simulates IO-saturation on one node to verify routing and autoscaler behavior.
estimated_impact: Approximately 35% sustained throughput reduction for AcmeRetail during the 45-minute recovery window; estimated revenue impact unknown (customer flagged production API).
notes: This ticket surfaces a new class of noisy-neighbor failure where node-level host IO, not raw GPU memory/compute, causes effective capacity loss. Allocator and autoscaler should correlate slot availability with attach/health signals to avoid silent capacity illusions.
